requirements.title: Configuration and scope of control
requirements.rationale: Push control must touch only registered patch branches of carry-patch workspaces and must follow variable changes on the next push.

criteria.action: treat PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN as enabled only when its value is exactly the case-sensitive string true, and as disabled when it is unset, has any other value (including True and 1), or its lookup returns an error
criteria.contract: only 'true' yields enabled; every other input including the lookup error yields disabled

setup: a GetVariableFunc stub returning controlled values
check.pseudocode: table: {unset:false,'true':true,'True':false,'1':false,err:false}; for each: assert pushPatchesEnabled(get)==expected

criteria.action: read PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE with the helper provided by spec 20_fork_patch_sync, so that unset, unrecognised and lookup-error values mean hub, and read both variables through GetVariableFunc for each ref update the control applies to, so a variable change takes effect on the next push without a restart
criteria.contract: unset, unrecognised and error values behave as hub (no rejection); after PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE changes to origin the very next push is rejected without restarting anything; both variables are read once per controlled ref update

setup: a counting GetVariableFunc over a real variable store
a registered patch branch in a carry_patch workspace
check.pseudocode: push1 ok under unset; set(PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE,'origin'); push2 rejected; assert getCalls per update >= 2 for both names

criteria.condition: a ref update targets refs/heads/<name> in a workspace whose workspace_mode is carry_patch, and <name> equals the branch_name of a patches row of that workspace with a status other than deleted, and <name> is not the workspace integration_branch
criteria.action: apply push control to that ref update
criteria.contract: each call returns a non-nil rejection error showing control applied

setup: a carry_patch workspace with integration_branch 'main-int' and patches rows with statuses active, pending and conflict
source origin with forwarding off
check.pseudocode: for b in [active,pending,conflict]: assert hook(ctx,db,slug,actor,update(refs/heads/+b)) != nil

criteria.condition: a ref update targets a branch whose patches row has status deleted, the integration branch (even if a patches row of that name exists), a branch with no patches row, a tag or any ref outside refs/heads/, or any ref of a standard-mode workspace
criteria.action: let the update through exactly as before this spec
criteria.contract: the hook returns nil, no origin push occurs, and the hub writes the ref

setup: source origin, forwarding on, a recording origin push function and a bare origin
a carry_patch workspace with a patch row status deleted, a patch row named like the integration branch, and a standard workspace
check.pseudocode: for u in cases: assert hook(u)==nil; assert originRefs(bare)==[]

criteria.condition: the workspace is in standard mode
criteria.action: read neither PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN nor PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE
criteria.contract: GetVariableFunc is called zero times for that push

setup: a standard-mode workspace
a GetVariableFunc stub counting calls
check.pseudocode: assert hook(...)==nil; assert getVarCalls==0

requirements.title: Pre-receive hook in the git server
requirements.rationale: Forwarding needs the unpacked commit but must precede the hub ref write, which only a hook at the ref-write step of the receive session provides.

criteria.action: expose RegisterPreReceiveHook(fn PreReceiveHookFunc) in the style of RegisterPostPushHook, where registering nil clears the hook and, with no hook registered, the receive-pack flow behaves as before this spec
criteria.contract: all three pushes succeed; after each push the trunk ref holds the pushed commit; the cleared rejecting hook is no longer consulted

setup: a gitserver test env
check.pseudocode: push -> assert ref==sha1; Register(allowAll); push -> assert ref==sha2; Register(rejectAll); Register(nil); push -> assert ref==sha3

criteria.condition: a receive-pack request contains ref updates and a pre-receive hook is registered
criteria.action: call the hook once per ref update (create, update or delete) in command order, after the pack is unpacked into the trunk and before the hub writes that ref, passing a context bound to the request, the *sql.DB, the workspace slug, the actor identity from apikit.GetAuthInfo (nil-safe) and the update (ref name, old hash, new hash)
criteria.contract: the hook is called exactly three times; calls arrive in the same order as the commands; each call carries slug, a non-nil context that is cancelled when the request ends, the *sql.DB, actor u1 and the ref name, old hash and new hash of its command; at call time the new commit object is already readable from the trunk and the ref has not yet been written; with an unauthenticated test context the actor argument is nil-safe and the hook is still called

setup: a recording pre-receive hook that returns nil
an authenticated request with apikit.AuthInfo for user u1 injected by the middleware
a push that creates branch a, updates branch b and deletes branch c
check.pseudocode: calls=[]; hook=func(ctx,db,slug,actor,upd){ calls=append(calls,{slug,actor,upd,hasObj(trunk,upd.New),refVal(trunk,upd.Name)}); return nil }; push(a,b,c); assert names(calls)==['a','b','c']; assert calls[0].hasObj

criteria.condition: the pre-receive hook returns a non-nil error for a ref update
criteria.action: not write or remove that ref and use the error text as the per-ref status message
criteria.contract: the ref keeps its old value; the client receives unpack ok and a per-ref ng <ref> <error text>, which git push shows as remote rejected with that message

setup: a gitserver test env from newGitTestEnv with a real trunk and the handler served over HTTP
a pre-receive hook registered that rejects every update with the text 'nope: blocked'
a local clone with one new commit on branch feature
check.pseudocode: RegisterPreReceiveHook(func(...) error { return errors.New('nope: blocked') }); out, err := gitPush(clone, 'feature'); assert err != nil; assert contains(out,'remote rejected'); assert contains(out,'nope: blocked'); assert refMissing(trunk,'refs/heads/feature')

criteria.condition: a push contains several ref updates and the hook rejects some of them and the other updates are not rejected
criteria.action: write the non-rejected refs and report each ref with its own status
criteria.contract: the non-rejected refs are written, the rejected refs are unchanged, and the client output contains the message of the rejected refs only

setup: a hook that rejects refs/heads/blocked with 'blocked by policy' and accepts refs/heads/open
a clone with commits on both branches
check.pseudocode: push(both); assert ref(open)==sha; assert ref(blocked)==old; assert out contains 'blocked by policy'; assert not rejectedLine(out,'open')

criteria.condition: the pre-receive hook returns nil for a ref update
criteria.action: let the hub write (or remove) the ref
criteria.contract: the ref holds the new value after the push

criteria.action: consult the hook from the wrapper around the trunk storer on every reference write and removal, keep that wrapper hiding PackfileWriter so thin packs resolve, receive per-request context and actor from the receive-pack handler, and import no code from internal/carrypatch
criteria.contract: each reference-writing and removing method calls the hook exactly once before delegating; a hook error is returned and the underlying storer is not modified; the wrapper does not expose a PackfileWriter method (type assertion to storer.PackfileWriter fails); go list -deps for internal/gitserver contains no internal/carrypatch package

setup: thinPackSafeStorer wrapping a real repo storer with a recording hook bound to a request context and actor
check.pseudocode: w := thinPackSafeStorer{...}; _,ok := any(w).(storer.PackfileWriter); assert !ok; assert w.SetReference(ref)==hookErr when hook rejects; deps := goListDeps('./internal/gitserver'); assert none contains 'internal/carrypatch'

requirements.title: Reject mode (origin source, forwarding off)
requirements.rationale: Without forwarding, an accepted hub push is a second writer that the next sync would replace or report, so the push is refused.

criteria.condition: a create or update of a registered patch branch is pushed and PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE resolves to origin and PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN is not true
criteria.action: reject the update with the message "branch is synced from origin; push to <git_url> instead"
criteria.contract: the hub ref is unchanged and the client sees the per-ref message

setup: carry_patch workspace, git_url https://example.com/fork.git, PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin, PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN unset
registered patch branch 'p1' existing at commit A on the hub
check.pseudocode: assert contains(out,'branch is synced from origin; push to https://example.com/fork.git instead'); assert ref(p1)==A; assert refMissing(p2)

criteria.action: for any workspaces.git_url value containing user:password@ userinfo, produce a rejection message in which the userinfo is removed and no credential text appears
criteria.contract: the message is 'branch is synced from origin; push to https://example.com/fork.git instead'; the message contains neither 'user' as credential nor 's3cret' nor '@'

setup: workspaces.git_url 'https://user:s3cret@example.com/fork.git'
reject mode applies
check.pseudocode:
err := hook(...); assert err.Error()=='branch is synced from origin; push to https://example.com/fork.git instead'
for url in gen_urls_with_userinfo(): msg := hook(...).Error(); assert !contains(msg, password); assert msg == fmt('branch is synced from origin; push to %s instead', stripUserinfo(url))

criteria.condition: a delete of a registered patch branch is pushed and PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE resolves to origin and PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN is not true
criteria.action: reject the delete with the same message as a create or update
criteria.contract: the hub branch still exists after the push

setup: reject mode, registered patch branch p1 present on the hub
check.pseudocode: out := gitPush(':refs/heads/p1'); assert contains(out,'branch is synced from origin'); assert ref(p1)==old

criteria.condition: one push contains a registered patch branch, an unregistered branch and a tag and reject mode applies
criteria.action: reject only the registered patch branch
criteria.contract: the unregistered branch and the tag are written and only the registered branch shows remote rejected

setup: reject mode
commits for registered branch p1, unregistered branch feature and tag v1
check.pseudocode: out := push(p1,feature,v1); assert rejectedRefs(out)==['refs/heads/p1']; assert ref(feature)&&tag(v1)

criteria.condition: the hook rejects a ref update in reject mode
criteria.action: log the rejection at info level with the slug, branch and pushing user ID (or unknown when there is no auth info)
criteria.contract: the push as a whole returns HTTP 200 with the per-ref error in the report

setup: reject mode
a captured logger
authenticated user id 'u-42', and a second run with no auth info
check.pseudocode: resp := post(...); assert resp.Status==200; rec := logs.Find(INFO,'rejected'); assert rec.slug && rec.branch && rec.user=='u-42'

requirements.title: Forward mode (origin source, forwarding on)
requirements.rationale: Forwarding to the fork before the hub writes its ref keeps the fork and the hub from disagreeing because of a hub push.

criteria.condition: a create or update of a registered patch branch is pushed and PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE resolves to origin and PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN is true
criteria.action: push the new commit to refs/heads/<name> on the trunk's origin remote with Force false and no + in the refspec before the hub writes its own ref, treating an already-up-to-date result as success
criteria.contract: on success the hook returns nil, the hub writes its ref, and the branch exists at the same commit on the fork and the hub

setup: trunk's origin remote is a local bare repository
source origin, PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN=true, registered patch branch p1
check.pseudocode: push(A); assert ref(trunk,p1)==A && ref(bare,p1)==A; push(B); assert both==B; seedOrigin(C); push(C); assert ok

criteria.action: push from a commit not yet referenced by a hub ref through a temporary ref under refs/hub/forward/<branch> (or a hash source if go-git supports one) and remove that temporary ref after both success and failure
criteria.contract: after each, no ref under refs/hub/forward/ exists in the trunk; during the forward the push is made from the temporary ref or a hash source that resolves the unreferenced commit

setup: forward mode with a local bare origin
check.pseudocode: push(ok); assert refsWithPrefix(trunk,'refs/hub/forward/')==[]; push(nonff); assert refsWithPrefix(trunk,'refs/hub/forward/')==[]

criteria.action: resolve origin credentials with workspace.ResolveCloneAuth (GIT_PAT, then GIT_USERNAME/GIT_PASSWORD, then none) and bound each forward by a 120 second timeout
criteria.contract: the resolver is called with the workspace slug; PushOptions has RemoteName origin, Force false and a refspec with no leading '+'; the context passed to the push has a deadline about 120 seconds from now

setup: an injected credential resolver recording its calls and a push function seam recording PushOptions and context
check.pseudocode: opts, ctx := captured; assert opts.Force==false; assert !startsWith(opts.RefSpecs[0],'+'); assert 119s < deadline(ctx)-now <= 120s

criteria.condition: origin credential resolution fails
criteria.action: reject the ref without contacting origin
criteria.contract: the per-ref message is "failed to resolve origin credentials" and the hub ref is unchanged

setup: forward mode
a resolver returning an error
a bare origin
check.pseudocode: err := hook(...); assert err.Error()=='failed to resolve origin credentials'; assert originRefs==[]

criteria.condition: the forward fails (non-fast-forward, authentication, network error or the 120 second timeout)
criteria.action: reject the update and not write the hub ref
criteria.contract: the per-ref message is "origin rejected push: <error>" with URL userinfo removed from <error>, the hub ref is unchanged and the fork is unchanged

setup: forward mode with a local bare origin whose p1 has moved ahead with a commit the hub lacks
hub p1 at commit A
forward mode where the origin remote URL is a nonexistent path or URL containing user:pw@
a captured logger
check.pseudocode:
out := push(B); assert contains(out,'origin rejected push: '); assert ref(trunk,p1)==A; assert ref(bare,p1)==originTip
out := push(); assert contains(out,'origin rejected push: '); assert !contains(out,'pw'); rec := logs.Find(WARN); assert rec.slug && rec.branch && rec.user && !contains(rec.error,'pw')

criteria.condition: a forward fails
criteria.action: log at warn level the slug, branch, pushing user and the error with URL userinfo removed

criteria.condition: a delete of a registered patch branch is pushed and PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE resolves to origin and PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN is true
criteria.action: reject the delete without contacting origin
criteria.contract: the per-ref message is "branch is synced from origin; delete it on the fork instead" and neither the hub branch nor the fork branch is deleted

setup: forward mode, p1 exists on both hub and local bare origin
check.pseudocode: out := push(':p1'); assert contains(out,'branch is synced from origin; delete it on the fork instead'); assert exists(trunk,p1)&&exists(bare,p1)

criteria.condition: one push contains a registered patch branch to forward and a ref the control does not apply to and forward mode applies
criteria.action: forward only the registered patch branch and let the other ref through unchanged
criteria.contract: both refs are written on the hub and only the patch branch exists on the fork

setup: forward mode with local bare origin
registered p1 and unregistered feature
check.pseudocode: push(p1,feature); assert ref(trunk,p1)&&ref(trunk,feature); assert exists(bare,p1); assert !exists(bare,feature)

requirements.title: Accepted refs only drive side effects
requirements.rationale: A ref that failed to update must not trigger rebuilds, audit entries or head_sha changes.

criteria.action: classify a ref update as accepted when its entry in the report status is ok, or, when no report status is available, unless the pre-receive hook rejected it
criteria.contract: with the report only a is accepted; with no report, every command except c is accepted

setup: a ReportStatus with entries ok for refs/heads/a and an error string for refs/heads/b
a nil report with a hook-rejected set containing refs/heads/c
check.pseudocode: assert names(accepted(cmds,rs,nil))==['a']; assert names(accepted(cmds,nil,{c}))==['a','b']

criteria.condition: a push finishes with at least one accepted update
criteria.action: give emitGitPushAudit only the accepted commands and invoke the post-push hook with extractPushedBranches of the accepted commands only, keeping deletes excluded
criteria.contract: refs_updated in the hub.git.push event lists accepted refs only and the hook receives accepted branches only

setup: a hook rejecting refs/heads/p1
a recording post-push hook and audit emitter
a deletion of refs/heads/old included in the push and accepted
check.pseudocode: push(p1,feature,':old'); assert postHookBranches==['feature']; assert 'refs/heads/p1' not in event.refs_updated; assert 'refs/heads/feature' in event.refs_updated

criteria.condition: no ref update of a push was accepted
criteria.action: emit no hub.git.push event and run no post-push hook
criteria.contract: no rebuild job is enqueued and the audit log gains no entry for the push

setup: reject mode with the real carry-patch post-push hook and a job queue
a recording audit emitter
check.pseudocode: push(p1); wait(); assert events==[]; assert hookCalls==0; assert queue.len()==0

criteria.action: leave updateHeadSHA unchanged, reading the trunk HEAD, for every push
criteria.contract: head_sha equals the trunk HEAD after the accepted push; after the rejected-only push head_sha equals the current trunk HEAD (unchanged and harmless)

setup: a workspace whose head_sha is stale
a trunk whose HEAD changed through an accepted push, and a second rejected-only push
check.pseudocode: push(ok); assert db.head_sha==trunkHEAD; push(rejected); assert db.head_sha==trunkHEAD

criteria.action: for any push, including pushes whose refs failed to update for reasons unrelated to patch branches, invoke the post-push hook and emit the audit event for a subset of the accepted ref updates only, never for a ref whose status is not ok
criteria.contract: the audited refs and the post-push branches are subsets of the ok commands; no command with non-ok status ever appears in either; no event is emitted when the ok set is empty

setup: a stub receive session producing arbitrary per-command statuses
check.pseudocode: for cmds,statuses in gen(): accepted := classify(cmds,statuses); assert set(audited) <= set(ok(cmds,statuses)); assert set(postBranches) <= set(branchesOf(ok)); assert (len(ok)==0) == (eventsEmitted==0)

requirements.title: Hub-mode mirror (hub source, forwarding on)
requirements.rationale: In hub mode the hub is authoritative and the fork should receive its patch branches on a best-effort basis.

criteria.condition: a push that created or updated a registered patch branch was accepted and PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE resolves to hub and PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN is true
criteria.action: force-push the branch's current hub tip to origin with the refspec +refs/heads/<name>:refs/heads/<name>, credentials resolved as in 22-REQ-4.3 and a 120 second timeout
criteria.contract: the branch exists on the fork at the hub tip, including after a rewrite of the branch

setup: hub mode (source unset), PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN=true, local bare origin, registered patch branch p1
post-push hook built with credential resolver, workspace root and emitter
check.pseudocode: hook(db,slug,['p1']); assert ref(bare,p1)==ref(trunk,p1); rewrite(); hook(db,slug,['p1']); assert ref(bare,p1)==newTip

criteria.action: run the rebuild enqueue first, unchanged, and then the mirror in the same goroutine, whether the rebuild was enqueued, suppressed by AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH=false, or deduplicated
criteria.contract: in the enqueue scenario the enqueue is observed before the origin push; with AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH=false no job is enqueued but origin receives p1; with a deduplicated enqueue origin still receives p1; both happen in the single hook goroutine

setup: hub mode with forwarding on, a recording queue and a local bare origin
scenarios: rebuild enqueued, AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_PUSH=false, deduplicated enqueue
check.pseudocode: order := recordOrder(queue, originPush); assert order==['enqueue','mirror']; setVar(AUTO,'false'); run; assert queue.len()==0 && exists(bare,p1)

criteria.condition: the mirror of one branch fails or the rebuild enqueue fails
criteria.action: continue with the remaining branches and the mirror respectively, with no retry and no persisted state
criteria.contract: the push still returns success, the rebuild enqueue is not prevented by a mirror failure, and the other branches of the push are mirrored

setup: hub mode with forwarding on
a local bare origin with a pre-receive hook refusing branch p2
two registered branches p1 and p2 in one push
a second run where the queue enqueue returns an error
check.pseudocode: hook(db,slug,['p1','p2']); assert queue.len()==1; assert exists(bare,p1) && !exists(bare,p2); queue.failNext(); hook(...); assert exists(bare,p1)

criteria.condition: PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN is not true, the source resolves to origin, the branch is unregistered or the integration branch, or the workspace is in standard mode
criteria.action: not mirror the branch
criteria.contract: the fork receives no push for that branch

setup: a local bare origin
registered branch p1 and the integration branch in a carry_patch workspace and a standard workspace
check.pseudocode: for case in cases: setup(case); hook(db,slug,[branch]); assert originRefs(bare)==[]

criteria.action: not mirror branch deletions, because extractPushedBranches excludes deletes
criteria.contract: the post-push hook receives no branches for the delete; origin p1 is not deleted

setup: hub mode with forwarding on and p1 present on the origin
check.pseudocode: push(':p1'); assert hookBranches==[]; assert exists(bare,p1)

criteria.condition: the origin-credentials resolver, workspace root and audit emitter are supplied to NewPostPushRebuildHook
criteria.action: perform the mirror, and with any of those dependencies nil, disable the mirror and leave the rebuild behaviour as before this spec
criteria.contract: with all supplied origin receives the branch; with any one nil origin receives nothing and the rebuild job is still enqueued as before with SubmittedBy system:push-hook

setup: hub mode with forwarding on and a local bare origin
check.pseudocode: for deps in [all, nilResolver, emptyRoot, nilEmitter]: hook := New(queue,get,deps...); hook(db,slug,['p1']); assert queue.len()==1; assert exists(bare,p1)==(deps==all)

requirements.title: Mirror failure event and logging
requirements.rationale: A best-effort mirror needs visible failures without affecting the push.

criteria.condition: a hub-mode mirror of a branch fails
criteria.action: emit the audit event hub.patch.mirror_failed with resource_type patch, action mirror, actor_type system, the workspace slug and metadata {branch_name, error}
criteria.contract: the error value in metadata has URL userinfo removed

setup: a recording emitter and an origin whose error text contains https://user:pw@host/repo.git
check.pseudocode: ev := emitter.events[0]; assert ev.Type=='hub.patch.mirror_failed'; assert ev.ResourceType=='patch' && ev.Action=='mirror' && ev.ActorType=='system'; assert ev.Metadata.branch_name=='p1'; assert !contains(ev.Metadata.error,'pw')

criteria.action: define the hub.patch.mirror_failed event type as a constant in internal/audit/types.go next to EventRebuildFollowup
criteria.contract: the constant's value is 'hub.patch.mirror_failed'; it is declared adjacent to EventRebuildFollowup

setup: internal/audit/types.go
check.pseudocode: assert audit.EventPatchMirrorFailed=='hub.patch.mirror_failed'; assert adjacent(src,'EventRebuildFollowup','hub.patch.mirror_failed')

criteria.condition: a mirror succeeds
criteria.action: log at info level and emit no event
criteria.contract: no hub.patch.mirror_failed event is emitted

setup: a captured logger and a recording emitter
a working local bare origin and a failing origin
check.pseudocode: mirror(good); assert logs.Has(INFO) && emitter.events==[]; mirror(bad); assert logs.Find(WARN).slug && .branch && .error

criteria.condition: a mirror fails
criteria.action: log at warn level the slug, branch and error

criteria.condition: the audit emitter is nil or its emit call returns an error
criteria.action: skip emission when nil, or log the emit error, and change nothing else
criteria.contract: the mirror outcome, the remaining mirrors and the rebuild enqueue are unaffected

setup: hub mode with forwarding on, branches p1 (failing) and p2 (succeeding)
one run with an emitter returning an error on every emit and one run with a nil emitter passed through a test seam
check.pseudocode: run(errEmitter); assert exists(bare,p2) && queue.len()==1; assert logs.Has('emit'); run(nilEmitter); assert exists(bare,p2)

requirements.title: Failure and boundary behaviour
requirements.rationale: Deciding whether to control a push fails open so the default hub mode is never blocked by a database error, while forward failures fail closed.

criteria.condition: determining whether control applies fails (workspace-mode query, variable lookup beyond the defaults in 22-REQ-1, or patch registration query)
criteria.action: let the update through and log a warning
criteria.contract: the hook returns nil and the hub writes the ref

setup: a carry_patch workspace with source origin
stubs that fail one at a time: the workspace-mode query, a variable lookup returning an unexpected failure beyond defaults, and the patches registration query
check.pseudocode: for failure in [modeQuery,patchQuery,variableErr]: assert hook(...)==nil; assert logs.Has(WARN)

criteria.condition: a forward fails
criteria.action: never accept the update silently
criteria.contract: the hook returns a non-nil error and the hub ref is not written

criteria.condition: a client does not request report-status
criteria.action: still reject the update the hook rejected
criteria.contract: the hub ref is unchanged and the client receives no per-ref message

setup: a hook that rejects refs/heads/feature with 'denied here'
a hand-built receive-pack request body without the report-status capability
check.pseudocode: body := encodeUpdateRequest(cmds, caps=[]); resp := post(body); assert ref(feature)==old; assert !contains(resp.body,'denied here')

criteria.condition: a receive-pack request has an empty body (no-op push)
criteria.action: not call the pre-receive hook
criteria.contract: the response is the existing no-op response; the hook call count is 0

setup: a counting pre-receive hook
check.pseudocode: post(emptyBody); assert hookCalls==0

criteria.action: leave the info/refs advertisement, clone and fetch unchanged, and leave pushes to unregistered branches, the integration branch, tags, other refs and standard-mode workspaces unchanged
criteria.contract: the advertisement, clone and fetch succeed with the same refs as before; every one of those pushes succeeds and the refs are written; no origin push occurs

setup: the carry-patch pre-receive hook registered
a carry_patch workspace with PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin and a standard workspace
a registered patch branch in the carry_patch workspace
check.pseudocode: assert advertise ok; clone ok; for ref in [feature,integration,tag v1,refs/notes/x]: assert push(ref).ok && ref written; assert push(stdBranch).ok

criteria.action: not recover a panicking pre-receive hook specially, leaving the existing handler behaviour in force
criteria.contract: the handler adds no recover of its own; the outcome is the same as for any other handler panic (existing behaviour); no accepted-ref side effects (audit event, post-push hook) occur

setup: a hook that panics
the handler mounted the same way as in existing tests (with the framework's normal recovery behaviour)
check.pseudocode: Register(panicHook); assertPanicHandledLikeOtherHandlers(push()); assert auditCount==0 && postHookCalls==0

requirements.title: Wiring, documentation and tests
requirements.rationale: Project steering requires docs and wiring in the same change, and the PRD requires local-bare-repository tests for every behaviour.

criteria.action: register the carry-patch pre-receive hook with gitserver.RegisterPreReceiveHook and build the post-push hook with the origin-credentials resolver, workspace root and audit emitter, using store.GetVariableValue, workspace.ResolveCloneAuth and the existing audit emitter, apikit helpers for timestamps and auth info, and no local auth structs
criteria.contract: the origin-mode push is rejected with the origin message (pre-receive hook registered); the hub-mode push reaches the local bare origin (post-push hook has mirror dependencies); the wiring source uses store.GetVariableValue and workspace.ResolveCloneAuth and declares no local auth struct

setup: the app wiring function from cmd/af-hub run against a test database and temporary workspace root
check.pseudocode: app := wire(); assert contains(push(origin mode),'branch is synced from origin'); assert exists(bare,p1) after hub-mode push

criteria.action: list PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN in the Workspace Variables Reference, describe in the git-server push section the three behaviours, the per-ref messages and the accepted-refs-only rule, and document the hub.patch.mirror_failed event
criteria.contract: the Workspace Variables Reference lists PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN; the git push section mentions 'branch is synced from origin; push to', 'origin rejected push:', 'failed to resolve origin credentials' and accepted refs only; hub.patch.mirror_failed is documented

setup: docs/api.md

leaves the hub ref unchanged, reports unpack ok and ng for the ref, emits no hub.git.push event and runs no post-push hook
